study_info.title: Robotic versus conventional nipple sparing mastectomy and immediate gel implant breast reconstruction in the management of breast cancer- A case control comparison study with analysis of clinical outcome, medical cost, and patient-reported cosmetic results
study_info.authors: Hung-Wen Lai, Shou-Tung Chen, Chi Wei Mok, Ying-Jen Lin, Hwa-Koon Wu, Shih-Lung Lin, Dar-Ren Chen, Shou-Jen Kuo
study_info.journal: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery
study_info.study_design: Retrospective, non-randomized, case-control comparison study conducted at a single institution
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Patients with primary operable breast cancer who underwent NSM from July 2011 to September 2019; only patients who received immediate direct to cohesive gel implant breast reconstructions; for R-NSM: early stage breast cancer (carcinoma in situ, stage I - IIIA), tumor size less than 5 cm, no evidence of multiple lymph nodes metastases, and no evidence of nipple, skin, or chest wall invasion; ideal candidates for R-NSM are patients with small to medium sized, none to mildly ptotic breast (breast cup size C and below).
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Patients who had received previous breast conserving surgery or previous radiation to the chest wall; operations other than NSM; prophylactic mastectomy or indications other than malignancy/benign disease; patients without breast reconstructions or with breast reconstructions other than direct-to-cohesive gel implants; operations performed by surgeons other than Dr. Hung-Wen Lai; endoscopic assisted NSM cases; for R-NSM: apparent NAC involvement, inflammatory breast cancer, breast cancer with chest wall or skin invasion, locally advanced breast cancer, breast cancer with extensive axillary lymph nodes metastases (stage IIIB or later), and patients with severe co-morbid conditions (heart disease, renal failure, liver dysfunction, poor performance status); women with large (breast cup size larger than E or breast mastectomy weight >600 gm) and ptotic breast.
study_info.study_setting: Single tertiary medical center (Changhua Christian Hospital, Taiwan)
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Prospectively maintained breast cancer database at Changhua Christian Hospital
study_info.number_of_participants_analyzed: 116 procedures (54 R-NSM, 62 C-NSM); 51 patients (54 procedures) in R-NSM group, 62 patients (62 procedures) in C-NSM group
study_info.dropout_reasons: Not explicitly reported; however, 45 (72.6%) patients in the C-NSM group and 50 (92.6%) in the R-NSM group completed the self-reported questionnaire.

minimal_units.arm_name: Robotic nipple sparing mastectomy (R-NSM) with immediate gel implant breast reconstruction (IGBR)
minimal_units.intervention_details: Robotic nipple sparing mastectomy (R-NSM) performed using the da Vinci surgical platform with three-dimensional imaging, through a 3–5 cm extra-mammary axillary or lateral chest incision, followed by immediate direct-to-cohesive silicone gel implant breast reconstruction placed in the sub-pectoral muscular pocket (pectoralis major, serratus anterior, and fascia of external oblique muscle) without acellular dermal matrix or mesh.

minimal_units.arm_name: Conventional nipple sparing mastectomy (C-NSM) with immediate gel implant breast reconstruction (IGBR)
minimal_units.control_details: Conventional nipple sparing mastectomy (C-NSM) performed by the same surgeon (HWL) with immediate direct-to-cohesive silicone gel implant breast reconstruction placed in the sub-pectoral muscular pocket (pectoralis major, serratus anterior, and fascia of external oblique muscle) without acellular dermal matrix or mesh. Incision types varied widely, typically 8–10 cm, in various locations including peri-areolar or infra-mammary incisions.
